synopsis: IEC TS 62998, alongside IEC 61496, provides an established certification basis for component-level detection capability in safety-rated sensors [f1038]. The glossary places these standards in the neighboring factory-safety sector and links them to demonstrating the reliability of contactless protective sensors, including light curtains, laser scanners and recently radar [f15276, f12388]. Qualifying sensors under these standards is presented as an approach to shortening validation of perception-dependent safety functions [f437]. The corpus nevertheless records a disagreement between keeping machine learning outside the safety function through certified deterministic sensing and accepting machine learning under ISO/PAS 8800-style assurance; sensor certification therefore represents one contested assurance approach, not a settled choice [f1125].

relations.note: Identifies sensor types and explains the reliability role of the certification standards.
Locates the established sensor-certification basis in the neighboring factory-safety sector.
Established component certification provides a basis for shortening perception-function validation.
Defined reliability demonstration supports using qualified sensors to shorten validation.
